sources.entry: SpaceMap - Disk usage analyzer that draws your disk as a nested treemap you can zoom into, filling in live while the scan runs. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/renkagod/spacemap) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: SpaceMap is a native macOS disk usage analyzer that draws the disk as a nested, zoomable treemap that fills in while the scan runs.
summary.what_it_does: It scans a folder or disk on all cores and draws folders as nested frames and files as tiles, sized like du (allocated blocks, hard links counted once, symlinks and other volumes skipped). Small items are merged into an "N more" block. You can double-click or pinch to zoom into folders and go back up with Esc, ⌘↑, the mouse back button or a swipe. A sidebar shows the current folder's contents, largest files and a breakdown by file type, and clicking a type dims everything else on the map. Right-click menus open files, reveal them in Finder, copy paths, rescan folders or move items to the Trash. The interface is in English and Russian, and new languages can be added without rebuilding.
use_cases: find what is taking up space on my Mac
visualize disk usage as a treemap
drill into nested folders to find large files
clean up large files before running out of disk space
check which file types use the most storage
how_to_run: Download SpaceMap-macOS.zip from Releases, unzip it and drag SpaceMap.app into Applications
If macOS blocks the first launch, run: xattr -cr /Applications/SpaceMap.app
Optionally grant Full Disk Access in System Settings → Privacy & Security to scan Mail, Messages and system folders
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd spacemap, then run: bash scripts/build-app.sh
notable: Live treemap that fills in while the scan is still running
Sizes match du: allocated blocks, hard links counted once
Packages like apps, Photos library and Logic projects shown as single blocks
Squarified treemap layout with nested folders
No third-party dependencies, only system frameworks
caveats: The app is not signed with an Apple certificate, so the first launch must be allowed manually or via xattr
Without Full Disk Access, some folders such as Mail and Messages show as inaccessible
keywords: see what takes space on mac
